bills.title: GRACE for Military Survivors Act
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: H.R. 9489 falls under Treasury's purview because it would modify survivor benefit tax provisions within the Internal Revenue Code, which is administered by the IRS under Treasury's authority. The implementation risk centers on IRS systems and guidance needing updates to correctly process changed exclusion or credit calculations for military survivor annuity recipients.

bills.title: Taxpayer Funds Oversight and Accountability Act
bills.status: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
bills.nexus: H.R. 8340 targets federal expenditure transparency and accountability mechanisms that fall under Treasury's Fiscal Service and the Office of Management and Budget's payment and reporting infrastructure. Treasury's implementation risk centers on potential new data-reporting mandates or audit requirements that could affect USASpending.gov systems and the Bureau of the Fiscal Service's disbursement and reconciliation operations.

bills.title: Pre-Payment Fraud Prevention and Treasury Data Access Act
bills.nexus: H.R. 8463 directly implicates the Bureau of the Fiscal Service and potentially the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN), as it governs pre-payment fraud controls and expands or restricts Treasury's authority to access and share payment data. The implementation risk centers on integrating new fraud-screening requirements into existing Fiscal Service disbursement systems while managing data governance obligations and potential conflicts with Privacy Act constraints.

bills.title: Agriculture, Rural Development, Food and Drug Administration, and Related Agency Appropriations Act, 2027
bills.nexus: H.R. 8646 funds the Food and Drug Administration, which operates under Treasury's interest as FDA fee collections and user-charge structures can intersect with OMB budget scoring and Treasury's cash management functions. Treasury's Office of Management and Budget liaison and the Fiscal Service should monitor any riders or rescissions that alter mandatory spending baselines or affect the Judgment Fund and other permanent appropriations.

bills.title: Making appropriations for military construction, the Department of Veterans Affairs, and related agencies for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2027, and for other purposes.
bills.nexus: Treasury's interest is limited here, as this bill primarily funds military construction and VA programs outside Treasury's direct jurisdiction, though the Office of Management and Budget coordinates with Treasury on budget scoring and any general provisions affecting appropriations or borrowing authority. The main risk angle is whether the bill contains any riders affecting debt issuance, tax expenditures, or rescissions that could intersect with Treasury's fiscal management responsibilities.

bills.title: Dietary Supplements Access Act
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: H.R. 8933 would expand the eligibility of dietary supplements as qualified medical expenses under Health Savings Accounts (HSAs) and Flexible Spending Arrangements (FSAs), directly implicating IRS authority under Sections 106, 213, and 223 of the Internal Revenue Code, which Treasury and IRS administer. Treasury faces implementation risk in defining eligible supplement categories, issuing guidance to plan administrators, and managing potential revenue loss from expanded tax-advantaged spending.

bills.title: To amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to modify certain investment credit rules with respect to nuclear facilities.
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: H.R. 8482 directly implicates IRS and Treasury's Office of Tax Policy because it proposes to amend IRC investment credit provisions governing nuclear facilities, which Treasury administers through guidance and rulemaking. The implementation risk centers on potential revenue cost, the need for updated Treasury/IRS regulations defining eligible facilities, and coordination with DOE on qualifying criteria.

bills.title: Big Oil Windfall Profits Tax Act
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: H.R. 7960 would impose an excise tax on major integrated oil companies' quarterly profits exceeding a baseline, directly implicating IRS's authority to administer and enforce a new excise regime under Treasury's Office of Tax Policy. Treasury faces significant implementation risk in defining "windfall profit" thresholds, designing quarterly reporting mechanisms, and coordinating with the IRS on compliance infrastructure for a novel tax structure.

bills.title: Buying American Cotton Act of 2026
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: Treasury cares because the bill is referred to Ways and Means, the primary jurisdiction for trade and tariff legislation, placing it squarely within Treasury's Office of International Affairs and the Office of the United States Trade Representative coordination lane. The implementation risk centers on any tariff schedule modifications or customs revenue impacts that would require Customs and Border Protection rulemaking and could affect trade agreement obligations Treasury monitors.

bills.title: Shutdown Fairness Act
bills.status: Referred to the Committee on Appropriations, and in addition to the Committees on Armed Services, Oversight and Government Reform, House Administration, and the Judiciary, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
bills.nexus: H.R. 7137 would require federal employees, including Treasury staff, to receive automatic pay continuation during a government shutdown, directly affecting Treasury's payroll operations and the Bureau of the Fiscal Service's payment processing authority. The implementation risk centers on Treasury's obligation to disburse salaries without an active appropriation, creating potential Antideficiency Act tension that the Office of General Counsel and the Fiscal Assistant Secretary would need to resolve.

bills.title: United States Foreign Service Commemorative Coin Act
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Financial Services.
bills.nexus: H.R. 6126 directs the Treasury Department, through the U.S. Mint (Bureau of the Mint authority under 31 U.S.C. § 5112), to design, mint, and issue commemorative coins honoring the U.S. Foreign Service. Treasury bears implementation responsibility for managing coin production, surcharge collection, and distribution logistics, along with the financial risk of unsold inventory if public demand falls short of projected mintage levels.

bills.title: Protecting America's Property Rights Act
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Financial Services.
bills.nexus: H.R. 3206 directly implicates the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency and federal banking regulators to the extent it restricts or conditions how federally chartered institutions can hold, finance, or transact in real property. Treasury must monitor implementation risk because any new constraints on property rights related to federally backed lending or collateral could affect credit availability, bank asset quality, and FHFA-overseen mortgage markets.

bills.title: Generating Retirement Ownership through Long-Term Holding
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: H.R. 2089 directly implicates the Office of Tax Policy and IRS authorities governing qualified retirement accounts, as it would alter holding-period or ownership rules tied to tax-advantaged retirement savings vehicles. Treasury's implementation risk centers on the need for regulatory guidance, potential revenue scoring implications, and IRS administrative burden in updating compliance and reporting frameworks.

bills.title: American CANS Act
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: H.R. 914 (American CANS Act) is before the Ways and Means Committee, placing it squarely within Treasury's jurisdiction through IRS's administration of any related tax provisions or incentive structures. Treasury's implementation concern centers on potential revenue impact and any compliance or enforcement obligations that would fall to IRS to operationalize.
